data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: adaptability
sections.summary: The ability to change your ideas, behaviour or approach in order to deal successfully with new or different situations.

senses.definition: the ability to change your behaviour or ideas to suit different situations
examples: Her adaptability made her the perfect candidate for a role that required constant change.

senses.definition: the quality of being able to adjust successfully to new environments or challenges
examples: The adaptability of the team allowed them to succeed even when the project changed direction completely.

answers.answer: Her adaptability made her an ideal choice for the international position, which changed frequently.
He showed great adaptability in the maths test and scored the highest mark in the entire class.
She had a lot of adaptability in her school bag that she used for the science project.
The adaptability was very comfortable and easy to carry from one classroom to the next.

sections.question: ambition
sections.summary: A strong desire to achieve something important or be successful; also a particular goal that you want to reach.

senses.definition: a strong desire to be successful, powerful or rich
examples: Her ambition to become a doctor drove her to study harder than anyone else in her year.

senses.definition: a particular goal or thing that you want to achieve
examples: One of his lifelong ambitions was to climb to the summit of Mont Blanc.

answers.answer: Her ambition to become a journalist pushed her to work harder than anyone in her class.
He had great ambition in his suitcase for the overnight school trip to the capital city.
She showed real ambition in her handwriting, which was always perfectly neat and well-formed.
His ambition was to forget the whole episode as quickly as possible and simply move on.

sections.question: anxiety
sections.summary: A feeling of worry, nervousness or fear about something that is happening or might happen; also a strong wish to do something.

senses.definition: a feeling of worry and fear, especially about the future or something uncertain
examples: She experienced intense anxiety before her final exams and found it difficult to sleep at night.

senses.definition: a strong wish or desire to do something
examples: His anxiety to please his parents led him to study a subject he had little interest in.

answers.answer: He managed his anxiety by breathing deeply and reminding himself how well he had prepared.
She felt great anxiety when her team scored the winning goal in the very last minute.
She had a lot of anxiety after finishing all her work well ahead of the deadline.
The teacher gave the class an anxiety to complete before the end of the week.

sections.question: confidence
sections.summary: The feeling of being certain about your own abilities or that something will happen as you expect; also trust in someone or something.

senses.definition: the belief that you can do things well and that other people respect you
examples: Her confidence grew significantly after she delivered her first successful public presentation.

senses.definition: a feeling of trust or certainty about someone or something
examples: The team's poor results have reduced public confidence in the manager's ability to lead.

answers.answer: Winning the regional competition gave her the confidence to enter the national championship.
He had great confidence in his bag, packed with everything he needed for the working day.
She gained more confidence and decided to stay in bed for another hour that morning.
The teacher gave a confidence to every student who had worked particularly hard that term.

sections.question: curiosity
sections.summary: A strong desire to know or learn about something; also something that is interesting because it is unusual or rare.

senses.definition: a strong desire to know or find out about something
examples: Her curiosity about the natural world led her to choose biology as her university subject.

senses.definition: an unusual or rare object or fact that is interesting to people
examples: The museum was full of historical curiosities that fascinated both young and old visitors.

answers.answer: His natural curiosity about how things work made him an excellent engineering student.
She showed great curiosity in completing the task as quickly as possible and leaving early.
He felt strong curiosity after the heavy meal and went straight to bed without studying.
The teacher handed out a curiosity to each student to investigate and complete at home.

sections.question: enthusiasm
sections.summary: A feeling of energetic interest in and excitement about something; great eagerness or passion for a subject or activity.

senses.definition: great excitement and interest in something, shown in the way you talk or behave
examples: The students' enthusiasm for the drama project was clear from the energy they put into every rehearsal.

answers.answer: The teacher was impressed by the students' enthusiasm for the topic and extended the lesson.
She showed great enthusiasm after the long and exhausting bus journey home from the museum.
He had enthusiasm in his pencil case that he always used during Friday afternoon art class.
The class received an enthusiasm from the teacher at the very start of the new school term.

sections.question: gratitude
sections.summary: The feeling of being thankful and appreciative towards someone who has helped or done something kind for you.

senses.definition: the feeling of being grateful and wanting to thank someone for their help or kindness
examples: She wrote a letter to express her gratitude to the mentor who had guided her throughout the year.

answers.answer: He expressed his gratitude to the teacher who had given up her lunch breaks to help him.
She felt great gratitude when her team scored the winning goal in the final minute of the match.
He showed his gratitude by shouting at his classmates when they failed to follow the instructions.
The teacher distributed gratitude to each student at the end of the school year ceremony.

sections.question: independence
sections.summary: The state of not being controlled by or needing the support of others; also the political freedom of a country from outside rule.

senses.definition: the state of not needing help or support from other people
examples: Moving abroad for the first time gave her a powerful sense of independence and self-belief.

senses.definition: the political freedom of a country from the control or rule of another country
examples: The country celebrated fifty years of independence with a national public holiday.

answers.answer: Studying abroad helped him develop a strong sense of independence for the first time in his life.
She showed great independence by asking the teacher for help with absolutely every single question.
He had a lot of independence in his backpack that he needed for the afternoon physics lesson.
The students felt independence after the long and tiring walk home from the sports centre.

sections.question: patience
sections.summary: The ability to wait for a long time or to accept problems and difficulties without becoming angry or upset.

senses.definition: the ability to stay calm and not become annoyed when dealing with problems or delays
examples: Learning a new language takes a great deal of patience, as progress can often feel slow.

senses.definition: the ability to keep doing something difficult for a long time without giving up
examples: It took years of patience and dedication before she finally published her first novel.

answers.answer: Teaching young children requires a great deal of patience as well as creativity and energy.
She had great patience in completing the task and finished it ten minutes ahead of everyone else.
He showed incredible patience in running the five-kilometre race and crossed the finish line first.
The teacher gave the class patience to work through quietly during the afternoon study period.

sections.question: resilience
sections.summary: The ability to recover quickly from difficult situations or setbacks; also the ability of a material to return to its original shape.

senses.definition: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties, setbacks or trauma
examples: Her resilience throughout the most challenging year of her life showed true strength of character.

senses.definition: the ability of a substance or material to return to its original shape after being bent or stretched
examples: The resilience of the material makes it ideal for use in products that are frequently under pressure.

answers.answer: Despite failing the exam twice, his resilience kept him focused and he passed on the third attempt.
She showed great resilience by memorising all the vocabulary from the very first lesson perfectly.
He felt resilience when he heard the good news about the examination being postponed.
The students demonstrated resilience by finishing the straightforward worksheet in under five minutes.
